newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Forrestania expects big nickel upgrade.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Forrestania expects big nickel upgrade.

text.p: Forrestania Gold NL expects to substantially upgrade the resource at its proposed Maggie Hays nickel project in Western Australia after identifying high-grade intercepts from an in-fill drilling program, managing director Barry Eldridge told Reuters on Thursday.
"They are very significant hits," Eldridge said.

Two recent holes returned 50 metres at 2.02 percent nickel, including 6.9 metres of massive sulphides at a grade of 5.17 percent nickel, and 41.2 metres at 1.82 percent nickel, including 5.05 metres of massive sulphides at a grade of 4.66 percent nickel, Forrestania said earlier on Thursday.

"Based on the new results, the project could see production over a 15-year mine life increased to between 250,000 and 300,000 tonnes of contained nickel, from the current estimate of around 180,000 tonnes," Eldridge said.
"We're looking to produce 16,000 to 18,000 tonnes per annum over a 15-year period," he said.
The orebody is contained within the Lake Johnston Joint Venture, which is 50 percent owned by Forrestania and 50 percent owned by South Africa's Gencor Ltd.

A third hole now being drilled has encountered a mineralised zone of 33.7 metres, including 7.74 metres of massive sulphides. Assays in the third hole are not yet available, but grades should be in the 2.0 to 2.5 percent range, it said.
"What these intersections mean to us ... it will result in a significant improvement to the resource and hopefully put us very close to our objective," Eldridge said.
A new resource will be calculated in the current quarter and a significant upgrade to the current resource of 11.9 million tonnes at 1.55 percent nickel is expected, Forrestania said.

The partners have accelerated work on the project and are spending A$8.7 million in the current financial year with the intention of commencing a bankable feasibility study in the September 1997 quarter, Forrestania said.
